1	// This file implements lossless archiving of one organization's audit
2	// export. AuditExport hands back detached in-memory records and the caller
3	// separately retains the checkpoint pinning them; an archive serializes the
4	// export so it can be saved to a file when the service instance ends and
5	// read back later, still paired with the caller's own checkpoint and still
6	// usable as the material for RecheckDecisionOffline.
7	//
8	// The format is a length-delimited binary encoding built by hand rather
9	// than encoding/json: JSON text cannot carry bytes that are not valid
10	// UTF-8 without silently replacing them with U+FFFD, which would collapse
11	// genuinely different content (a lone 0xFF, a lone 0xFE and a real U+FFFD)
12	// onto identical records and change their fingerprints. Every string is
13	// written from its exact bytes with a length prefix, and nil slices,
14	// non-nil empty slices and absent payloads are each marked explicitly.
15	//
16	// Integrity never comes from trust in the file. A decode reconstructs the
17	// records and then runs the same whole-material VerifyAudit chain check
18	// against the checkpoint the caller supplies independently; the checkpoint
19	// embedded in the archive is informational only and never authoritative.
20	package darksafe
21	
22	import (
23		"bytes"
24		"crypto/sha256"
25		"encoding/binary"
26		"errors"
27		"fmt"
28	)
29	
30	// ErrInvalidArchive means archive bytes are not a recognizable, complete,
31	// untampered audit archive: a foreign/truncated/trailing-byte framing, a
32	// failed checksum, or content that does not decode. Content-level failures
33	// (missing or mismatched organization, missing, out-of-order or modified
34	// records, a mismatched checkpoint) keep using ErrMissingOrganization and
35	// ErrInvalidRange exactly as the other audit entry points do.
36	var ErrInvalidArchive = errors.New("darksafe: invalid audit archive")
37	
38	// Archive framing:
39	//
40	//	magic   = archiveMagic
41	//	u32 BE  = byte length of the payload that follows
42	//	payload = archivePayloadLen bytes
43	//	32 bytes = SHA-256 checksum of payload
44	//
45	// A second archive concatenated to a first is trailing material, not a
46	// second frame: a read consumes exactly one frame and rejects any byte
47	// beyond it.
48	const archiveMagic = "darksafe-audit-archive-v1\n"
49	
50	const (
51		archiveTagBoolFalse byte = 0
52		archiveTagBoolTrue  byte = 1
53		archiveTagNil       byte = 0
54		archiveTagPresent   byte = 1
55	)
56	
57	// archiveWriter appends length-delimited fields to a byte buffer.
58	type archiveWriter struct {
59		buf []byte
60		err error
61	}
62	
63	func (w *archiveWriter) raw(data []byte) {
64		w.buf = append(w.buf, data...)
65	}
66	
67	// u32 writes a non-negative int as a big-endian uint32.
68	func (w *archiveWriter) u32(v int) {
69		if v < 0 || uint64(v) > 0xffffffff {
70			w.err = fmt.Errorf("%w: length out of range: %d", ErrInvalidArchive, v)
71			return
72		}
73		var b [4]byte
74		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(b[:], uint32(v))
75		w.buf = append(w.buf, b[:]...)
76	}
77	
78	func (w *archiveWriter) boolean(v bool) {
79		if v {
80			w.buf = append(w.buf, archiveTagBoolTrue)
81		} else {
82			w.buf = append(w.buf, archiveTagBoolFalse)
83		}
84	}
85	
86	// stringField writes a string from its exact memory bytes. Nothing is
87	// validated, replaced or normalized: a lone 0xFF reaches the output as
88	// itself and stays distinguishable from 0xFE and a genuine U+FFFD.
89	func (w *archiveWriter) stringField(s string) {
90		w.u32(len(s))
91		if w.err != nil {
92			return
93		}
94		w.buf = append(w.buf, s...)
95	}
96	
97	// writeList frames every length-counted list in the archive, whatever its
98	// item type: the subject-role and matched-policy string lists and the
99	// policy-change policy list all share this one shape. nil is one marker, a
100	// non-nil list is a presence marker, a count and one encoded item each, so
101	// nil, non-nil empty and populated lists stay distinct and element order is
102	// whatever the caller supplied. Keeping the framing here — rather than
103	// copied per item type — means a list-format change is made once instead of
104	// mirrored between the two list kinds.
105	func writeList[T any](w *archiveWriter, items []T, writeItem func(T)) {
106		if items == nil {
107			w.buf = append(w.buf, archiveTagNil)
108			return
109		}
110		w.buf = append(w.buf, archiveTagPresent)
111		w.u32(len(items))
112		for i := range items {
113			writeItem(items[i])
114		}
115	}
116	
117	// policy writes one Policy by walking the single policy field table, so the
118	// archive's field order is the fingerprint's order by construction. Even the
119	// fingerprint-optional ResourceID is always written here (empty included),
120	// so every field round trips on its own; its placement is fixed by the
121	// table and therefore cannot move a fingerprint boundary.
122	func (w *archiveWriter) policy(p Policy) {
123		for i := range policyFields {
124			f := &policyFields[i]
125			switch f.kind {
126			case policyFieldString, policyFieldOptionalString:
127				w.stringField(f.getString(p))
128			case policyFieldBool:
129				w.boolean(f.getBool(p))
130			}
131		}
132	}
133	
134	// change writes the policy-change payload, or a single absence marker:
135	// VerifyAudit only ever accepts a change payload on a policy-change record
136	// and its absence otherwise, but the distinction is encoded explicitly so
137	// decode never has to reconstruct a shape. A present payload walks the
138	// single policy-change field table, so the archive's field order is the
139	// fingerprint's order by construction and every change field round trips.
140	func (w *archiveWriter) change(c *PolicyChange) {
141		if c == nil {
142			w.buf = append(w.buf, archiveTagNil)
143			return
144		}
145		w.buf = append(w.buf, archiveTagPresent)
146		for i := range changeFields {
147			f := &changeFields[i]
148			switch f.kind {
149			case changeFieldInt:
150				w.u32(f.getInt(c))
151			case changeFieldPolicyList:
152				writeList(w, f.getPolicies(c), w.policy)
153			case changeFieldBool:
154				w.boolean(f.getBool(c))
155			}
156		}
157	}
158	
159	// decisionRecord writes the decision payload, or a single absence marker:
160	// VerifyAudit only ever accepts a decision payload on a decision record and
161	// its absence otherwise, but the distinction is encoded explicitly so decode
162	// never has to reconstruct a shape. A present payload walks the single
163	// decision field table, so the archive's field order is the fingerprint's
164	// order by construction and every request and decision field round trips.
165	func (w *archiveWriter) decisionRecord(d *DecisionRecord) {
166		if d == nil {
167			w.buf = append(w.buf, archiveTagNil)
168			return
169		}
170		w.buf = append(w.buf, archiveTagPresent)
171		for i := range decisionFields {
172			f := &decisionFields[i]
173			switch f.kind {
174			case decisionFieldString:
175				w.stringField(f.getString(d))
176			case decisionFieldStringList:
177				writeList(w, f.getList(d), w.stringField)
178			case decisionFieldBool:
179				w.boolean(f.getBool(d))
180			case decisionFieldInt:
181				w.u32(f.getInt(d))
182			}
183		}
184	}
185	
186	// EncodeAuditArchive serializes one complete audit export into savable
187	// bytes. org is the organization name, records is its complete chain from
188	// sequence 1 (a valid prefix ending at some historical sequence is enough,
189	// provided cp pins exactly that sequence), and cp is the checkpoint the
190	// caller separately retains. An organization with no records archives too:
191	// records is empty and cp is its sequence-0 genesis checkpoint.
192	//
193	// The whole material is validated exactly as VerifyAudit would before any
194	// bytes are returned: a missing organization is ErrMissingOrganization, and
195	// a missing, out-of-order or foreign record, modified content or checkpoint
196	// mismatch is ErrInvalidRange. On failure no archive bytes are returned.
197	// The checkpoint is carried in the archive for reference, but never stands
198	// in for the separately retained evidence: DecodeAuditArchive always
199	// validates against the checkpoint handed to it. The call is read-only:
200	// neither the records nor any service state are mutated and no audit record
201	// is appended.
202	func EncodeAuditArchive(org string, records []AuditRecord, cp Checkpoint) ([]byte, error) {
203		if org == "" {
204			return nil, ErrMissingOrganization
205		}
206		if err := VerifyAudit(org, records, cp); err != nil {
207			return nil, err
208		}
209	
210		pw := &archiveWriter{}
211		pw.stringField(org)
212		pw.u32(cp.EndSeq)
213		pw.stringField(cp.Fingerprint)
214		pw.u32(len(records))
215		for i := range records {
216			rec := &records[i]
217			// The outer record fields walk the single record field table, so
218			// the archive's record layout is the fingerprint envelope's layout
219			// — plus the record's own fingerprint, which the envelope excludes
220			// — by construction, and no outer field can be skipped or
221			// reordered here alone.
222			for j := range recordFields {
223				f := &recordFields[j]
224				switch f.kind {
225				case recordFieldString:
226					pw.stringField(f.getString(rec))
227				case recordFieldInt:
228					pw.u32(f.getInt(rec))
229				case recordFieldChange:
230					pw.change(f.getChange(rec))
231				case recordFieldDecision:
232					pw.decisionRecord(f.getDecision(rec))
233				}
234			}
235		}
236		if pw.err != nil {
237			return nil, pw.err
238		}
239		payload := pw.buf
240	
241		out := make([]byte, 0, len(archiveMagic)+4+len(payload)+sha256.Size)
242		out = append(out, archiveMagic...)
243		var lenBuf [4]byte
244		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(lenBuf[:], uint32(len(payload)))
245		out = append(out, lenBuf[:]...)
246		out = append(out, payload...)
247		sum := sha256.Sum256(payload)
248		out = append(out, sum[:]...)
249		return out, nil
250	}
251	
252	// archiveReader walks one payload without copying string contents: string
253	// fields are backed by the payload slice itself, which is owned by the
254	// decoder and never returned, so callers cannot mutate the input through
255	// the result.
256	type archiveReader struct {
257		data []byte
258		pos  int
259		err  error
260	}
261	
262	func (r *archiveReader) need(n int) bool {
263		if r.err != nil {
264			return false
265		}
266		if n < 0 || r.pos > len(r.data)-n {
267			r.err = fmt.Errorf("%w: truncated archive payload", ErrInvalidArchive)
268			return false
269		}
270		return true
271	}
272	
273	func (r *archiveReader) marker() byte {
274		if !r.need(1) {
275			return 0
276		}
277		b := r.data[r.pos]
278		r.pos++
279		return b
280	}
281	
282	func (r *archiveReader) u32() int {
283		if !r.need(4) {
284			return 0
285		}
286		v := int(binary.BigEndian.Uint32(r.data[r.pos : r.pos+4]))
287		r.pos += 4
288		return v
289	}
290	
291	// boundedCount reads a count and proves at least minBytesPerItem bytes
292	// remain per item, so a hostile payload cannot drive a huge allocation
293	// with a count its body could never satisfy.
294	func (r *archiveReader) boundedCount(minBytesPerItem int) int {
295		n := r.u32()
296		if r.err != nil {
297			return 0
298		}
299		if n < 0 || uint64(n)*uint64(minBytesPerItem) > uint64(len(r.data)-r.pos) {
300			r.err = fmt.Errorf("%w: implausible list count %d", ErrInvalidArchive, n)
301			return 0
302		}
303		return n
304	}
305	
306	func (r *archiveReader) boolean() bool {
307		switch r.marker() {
308		case archiveTagBoolTrue:
309			return true
310		case archiveTagBoolFalse:
311			return false
312		default:
313			if r.err == nil {
314				r.err = fmt.Errorf("%w: invalid boolean marker", ErrInvalidArchive)
315			}
316			return false
317		}
318	}
319	
320	func (r *archiveReader) stringField() string {
321		n := r.u32()
322		if r.err != nil {
323			return ""
324		}
325		if !r.need(n) {
326			return ""
327		}
328		// Conversion copies the bytes, so the result never aliases the input.
329		s := string(r.data[r.pos : r.pos+n])
330		r.pos += n
331		return s
332	}
333	
334	// readList reads one length-counted list framed by writeList, whatever its
335	// item type: both string lists and the policy list decode here. Every list
336	// kind gets the exact same framing checks — the nil/presence marker, the
337	// per-item byte floor before any allocation, and each item's own
338	// truncation/structure errors — so a hostile count can neither drive a
339	// disproportionate allocation nor deliver a partial list: once an item
340	// fails, the reader's sticky error fails the whole read.
341	// minBytesPerItem is the minimum an item could occupy (each string item
342	// carries one length word; a policy item carries six length words and a
343	// bool), and is used only to reject counts the remaining bytes could never
344	// satisfy.
345	func readList[T any](r *archiveReader, minBytesPerItem int, readItem func() T) []T {
346		switch r.marker() {
347		case archiveTagNil:
348			return nil
349		case archiveTagPresent:
350		default:
351			if r.err == nil {
352				r.err = fmt.Errorf("%w: invalid list marker", ErrInvalidArchive)
353			}
354			return nil
355		}
356		n := r.boundedCount(minBytesPerItem)
357		if r.err != nil {
358			return nil
359		}
360		items := make([]T, n)
361		for i := range items {
362			items[i] = readItem()
363		}
364		return items
365	}
366	
367	func (r *archiveReader) policy() Policy {
368		// Read fields in the single table's (write and fingerprint) order. The
369		// fingerprint-optional ResourceID is still a mandatory, fixed field on
370		// the archive, so it is read for every policy including the empty one.
371		var p Policy
372		for i := range policyFields {
373			f := &policyFields[i]
374			switch f.kind {
375			case policyFieldString, policyFieldOptionalString:
376				f.setString(&p, r.stringField())
377			case policyFieldBool:
378				f.setBool(&p, r.boolean())
379			}
380		}
381		return p
382	}
383	
384	func (r *archiveReader) change() *PolicyChange {
385		switch r.marker() {
386		case archiveTagNil:
387			return nil
388		case archiveTagPresent:
389		default:
390			if r.err == nil {
391				r.err = fmt.Errorf("%w: invalid change payload marker", ErrInvalidArchive)
392			}
393			return nil
394		}
395		// Read fields in the single table's (write and fingerprint) order, so a
396		// field can never be restored into the wrong member or skipped.
397		c := &PolicyChange{}
398		for i := range changeFields {
399			f := &changeFields[i]
400			switch f.kind {
401			case changeFieldInt:
402				f.setInt(c, r.u32())
403			case changeFieldPolicyList:
404				// A policy writes six length words (five strings plus
405				// ResourceID) and one bool byte at minimum.
406				f.setPolicies(c, readList(r, 6*4+1, r.policy))
407			case changeFieldBool:
408				f.setBool(c, r.boolean())
409			}
410		}
411		return c
412	}
413	
414	func (r *archiveReader) decisionRecord() *DecisionRecord {
415		switch r.marker() {
416		case archiveTagNil:
417			return nil
418		case archiveTagPresent:
419		default:
420			if r.err == nil {
421				r.err = fmt.Errorf("%w: invalid decision payload marker", ErrInvalidArchive)
422			}
423			return nil
424		}
425		// Read fields in the single table's (write and fingerprint) order, so a
426		// field can never be restored into the wrong member or skipped.
427		d := &DecisionRecord{}
428		for i := range decisionFields {
429			f := &decisionFields[i]
430			switch f.kind {
431			case decisionFieldString:
432				f.setString(d, r.stringField())
433			case decisionFieldStringList:
434				// Each string item carries at least one length word.
435				f.setList(d, readList(r, 4, r.stringField))
436			case decisionFieldBool:
437				f.setBool(d, r.boolean())
438			case decisionFieldInt:
439				f.setInt(d, r.u32())
440			}
441		}
442		return d
443	}
444	
445	// DecodeAuditArchive reads one archive produced by EncodeAuditArchive and
446	// returns records that can be handed directly to RecheckDecisionOffline.
447	// org is the organization the caller expects, and cp is the checkpoint the
448	// caller independently retained; the checkpoint embedded in the file is
449	// never treated as evidence, so even an archive carrying a plausible
450	// checkpoint only validates against the one supplied here.
451	//
452	// A missing organization is ErrMissingOrganization. Unrecognized framing,
453	// truncation, a trailing second archive or any other extra byte, a bad
454	// checksum, and undecodable content are ErrInvalidArchive. Records that
455	// decode but are missing, out of order, foreign to the organization,
456	// modified (including a record after the one the caller intends to review)
457	// or mismatched with the supplied checkpoint fail the whole read with
458	// ErrInvalidRange. Failure returns no records. A successful read only
459	// proves the material matches the checkpoint: an original decision that
460	// disagrees with a recomputed one is reported later by offline review, not
461	// treated as archive damage. The result is detached from archive (mutating
462	// one never reaches the other), and the call is read-only.
463	func DecodeAuditArchive(archive []byte, org string, cp Checkpoint) ([]AuditRecord, error) {
464		if org == "" {
465			return nil, ErrMissingOrganization
466		}
467		magicLen := len(archiveMagic)
468		if len(archive) < magicLen+4+sha256.Size || string(archive[:magicLen]) != archiveMagic {
469			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: unrecognized audit archive", ErrInvalidArchive)
470		}
471		pos := magicLen
472		payloadLen := int(binary.BigEndian.Uint32(archive[pos : pos+4]))
473		pos += 4
474		checksumEnd := pos + payloadLen
475		if payloadLen < 0 || checksumEnd+sha256.Size != len(archive) {
476			// A short frame is truncation; bytes beyond the one frame (a
477			// concatenated second archive, junk appended to a good file) are a
478			// framing failure too.
479			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: truncated or trailing audit archive bytes", ErrInvalidArchive)
480		}
481		payload := archive[pos:checksumEnd]
482		sum := sha256.Sum256(payload)
483		if !bytes.Equal(sum[:], archive[checksumEnd:checksumEnd+sha256.Size]) {
484			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: checksum mismatch", ErrInvalidArchive)
485		}
486	
487		r := &archiveReader{data: payload}
488		embeddedOrg := r.stringField()
489		embeddedEndSeq := r.u32()
490		embeddedFingerprint := r.stringField()
491		// Every record writes two payload markers, a sequence word, two
492		// fingerprint length words and org/kind length words: 22 bytes even
493		// when every string is empty.
494		n := r.boundedCount(22)
495		if r.err != nil {
496			return nil, r.err
497		}
498		records := make([]AuditRecord, 0, n)
499		for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
500			// Read the outer fields in the single record field table's (write
501			// and fingerprint) order, so a field can never be restored into
502			// the wrong member or skipped.
503			var rec AuditRecord
504			for j := range recordFields {
505				f := &recordFields[j]
506				switch f.kind {
507				case recordFieldString:
508					f.setString(&rec, r.stringField())
509				case recordFieldInt:
510					f.setInt(&rec, r.u32())
511				case recordFieldChange:
512					f.setChange(&rec, r.change())
513				case recordFieldDecision:
514					f.setDecision(&rec, r.decisionRecord())
515				}
516			}
517			records = append(records, rec)
518		}
519		if r.err != nil {
520			return nil, r.err
521		}
522		if r.pos != len(payload) {
523			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: %d unconsumed archive bytes", ErrInvalidArchive, len(payload)-r.pos)
524		}
525	
526		// Content checks reuse the exact audit-range validation the live export
527		// and offline review paths use, so an archive can never smuggle in a
528		// shape those entry points would reject.
529		if embeddedOrg != org {
530			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: archive organization %q does not match %q", ErrInvalidRange, embeddedOrg, org)
531		}
532		// The embedded checkpoint is informational; still, contradicting its own
533		// header means the payload was altered, and the authoritative check
534		// below always uses the caller's independently retained checkpoint.
535		if embeddedEndSeq != cp.EndSeq || embeddedFingerprint != cp.Fingerprint {
536			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: embedded checkpoint does not match the retained checkpoint", ErrInvalidRange)
537		}
538		if err := VerifyAudit(org, records, cp); err != nil {
539			return nil, err
540		}
541		return records, nil
542	}

1	// This file implements the organization-scoped audit chain. Every successful
2	// policy publish or rollback, and every Decide called with a non-empty
3	// decision organization, leaves an immutable record in that organization.
4	//
5	// Records carry an organization-local sequence starting at 1 and a SHA-256
6	// fingerprint that chains each record to the previous one. The genesis
7	// fingerprint binds the organization name, so records from another
8	// organization can never validate as part of this chain even when the
9	// sequence numbers and identifiers coincide.
10	package darksafe
11	
12	import (
13		"crypto/sha256"
14		"encoding/binary"
15		"encoding/hex"
16		"encoding/json"
17		"errors"
18		"fmt"
19	)
20	
21	// Audit record categories.
22	const (
23		// AuditPolicyChange is a successful publish or rollback.
24		AuditPolicyChange = "policy_change"
25		// AuditDecision is one Decide evaluation.
26		AuditDecision = "decision"
27	)
28	
29	// Sentinel errors for the audit entry points. Callers distinguish them
30	// with errors.Is; every one leaves state unchanged.
31	var (
32		// ErrInvalidPage means a page size or range argument was invalid.
33		ErrInvalidPage = errors.New("darksafe: invalid audit page")
34		// ErrInvalidRange means the upper bound is beyond what exists, the
35		// range is inverted, or a supplied fingerprint does not match.
36		ErrInvalidRange = errors.New("darksafe: invalid audit range")
37		// ErrAuditNotFound means no record exists at the requested sequence.
38		ErrAuditNotFound = errors.New("darksafe: audit record not found")
39		// ErrAuditNotADecision means the record at the sequence is not a
40		// decision record and therefore cannot be rechecked.
41		ErrAuditNotADecision = errors.New("darksafe: audit record is not a decision")
42	)
43	
44	// PolicyChange captures a successful publish or rollback.
45	type PolicyChange struct {
46		// Version is the newly created policy version.
47		Version int
48		// Policies is the full policy set of the new version.
49		Policies []Policy
50		// SourceVersion is the version copied by a rollback, and 0 for an
51		// ordinary publish.
52		SourceVersion int
53		// RolledBack reports whether the change was produced by Rollback.
54		RolledBack bool
55	}
56	
57	// DecisionRecord captures one Decide call: the full request and the
58	// decision actually returned.
59	type DecisionRecord struct {
60		Request  OrgRequest
61		Decision Decision
62	}
63	
64	// AuditRecord is one immutable entry in an organization's audit chain.
65	type AuditRecord struct {
66		Org      string
67		Seq      int // organization-local, starting at 1 and gapless
68		Kind     string
69		Change   *PolicyChange   // present when Kind == AuditPolicyChange
70		Decision *DecisionRecord // present when Kind == AuditDecision
71	
72		// PrevFingerprint is the fingerprint of the preceding record, or the
73		// genesis fingerprint for the first record.
74		PrevFingerprint string
75		// Fingerprint binds this record's full content to its predecessor.
76		Fingerprint string
77	}
78	
79	// rawEnvelopePrefix opens every raw-byte canonical encoding. It never
80	// coincides with the start of a JSON envelope (always '{'), so
81	// fingerprints from the two encodings live in collision-free spaces.
82	const rawEnvelopePrefix = "darksafe-audit-raw-v1\x00"
83	
84	// fingerprintTag delimits one field or nested value within the canonical
85	// binary encoding. Distinct tags keep two payloads that merely share
86	// adjacent bytes apart (e.g. ["ab",""] vs ["a","b"]).
87	type fingerprintTag byte
88	
89	const (
90		tagEnvelope fingerprintTag = iota + 1
91		tagSeq
92		tagString
93		tagStringList
94		tagBool
95		tagPolicy
96		tagPolicyList
97		tagChange
98		tagSubject
99		tagResource
100		tagDecision
101		tagDecisionRecord
102	)
103	
104	// fingerprintEncoder builds the canonical byte representation of an
105	// envelope. Unlike encoding/json it writes string contents byte-for-byte
106	// with an explicit length prefix, so strings carrying invalid UTF-8 stay
107	// distinguishable: encoding/json renders both a raw 0xFF byte and a raw
108	// 0xFE byte as the U+FFFD replacement rune, collapsing genuinely
109	// different content onto identical fingerprints.
110	type fingerprintEncoder struct {
111		buf []byte
112	}
113	
114	func (e *fingerprintEncoder) tag(t fingerprintTag) {
115		e.buf = append(e.buf, byte(t))
116	}
117	
118	func (e *fingerprintEncoder) int64Tag(t fingerprintTag, v int64) {
119		e.tag(t)
120		var b [8]byte
121		binary.BigEndian.PutUint64(b[:], uint64(v))
122		e.buf = append(e.buf, b[:]...)
123	}
124	
125	func (e *fingerprintEncoder) boolTag(t fingerprintTag, v bool) {
126		e.tag(t)
127		if v {
128			e.buf = append(e.buf, 1)
129		} else {
130			e.buf = append(e.buf, 0)
131		}
132	}
133	
134	// rawString tags and writes a string from its exact memory bytes. No
135	// validation, replacement or normalization is ever performed: an invalid
136	// UTF-8 byte reaches the hash unchanged.
137	func (e *fingerprintEncoder) rawString(s string) {
138		e.tag(tagString)
139		var b [4]byte
140		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(b[:], uint32(len(s)))
141		e.buf = append(e.buf, b[:]...)
142		e.buf = append(e.buf, s...)
143	}
144	
145	// writeRawList frames every length-counted list in the raw canonical
146	// encoding, whatever its item type: the subject-role and matched-policy
147	// string lists and the policy-change policy list all share this one shape.
148	// The tag identifies the list kind, then nil is one marker and a non-nil
149	// list is a presence marker, a count and one encoded item each, so nil,
150	// non-nil empty and populated lists stay distinct and element order is
151	// whatever the caller supplied. Keeping the framing here — rather than
152	// copied per item type — means a list-format change is made once instead of
153	// mirrored between the two list kinds.
154	func writeRawList[T any](e *fingerprintEncoder, t fingerprintTag, items []T, writeItem func(T)) {
155		e.tag(t)
156		if items == nil {
157			e.buf = append(e.buf, 0)
158			return
159		}
160		e.buf = append(e.buf, 1)
161		var b [4]byte
162		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(b[:], uint32(len(items)))
163		e.buf = append(e.buf, b[:]...)
164		for i := range items {
165			writeItem(items[i])
166		}
167	}
168	
169	// stringList preserves nil-vs-empty explicitly: in the JSON envelope a
170	// nil slice is "null" and a non-nil empty slice is "[]", so the raw
171	// encoding must keep the two shapes apart as well.
172	func (e *fingerprintEncoder) stringList(items []string) {
173		writeRawList(e, tagStringList, items, e.rawString)
174	}
175	
176	func (e *fingerprintEncoder) policy(p Policy) {
177		e.tag(tagPolicy)
178		// Field order, the Recursive boolean's position, and ResourceID being
179		// appended only when set all come from the single policy field table, so
180		// the fingerprint and the archive enumerate fields in exactly one place.
181		for i := range policyFields {
182			f := &policyFields[i]
183			switch f.kind {
184			case policyFieldString:
185				e.rawString(f.getString(p))
186			case policyFieldOptionalString:
187				// ResourceID participates only when set, pairing with its
188				// omitempty JSON tag, so the legacy fingerprint bytes are
189				// unchanged for resource-unrestricted policies.
190				if v := f.getString(p); v != "" {
191					e.rawString(v)
192				}
193			case policyFieldBool:
194				e.boolTag(tagBool, f.getBool(p))
195			}
196		}
197	}
198	
199	// policyList frames the full policy set with the shared list shape, under
200	// the policy-list tag so a policy set can never collide with a string list
201	// whose concatenated bytes happen to match.
202	func (e *fingerprintEncoder) policyList(policies []Policy) {
203		writeRawList(e, tagPolicyList, policies, e.policy)
204	}
205	
206	func (e *fingerprintEncoder) change(c *PolicyChange) {
207		e.tag(tagChange)
208		// A nil pointer is encoded as tagChange alone; a present value's
209		// fields follow immediately.
210		if c == nil {
211			return
212		}
213		// Field order comes from the single policy-change field table, so the
214		// fingerprint, the UTF-8 decision, the archive and the detaching copy
215		// enumerate fields in exactly one place. No change field is skipped.
216		for i := range changeFields {
217			f := &changeFields[i]
218			switch f.kind {
219			case changeFieldInt:
220				e.int64Tag(tagSeq, int64(f.getInt(c)))
221			case changeFieldPolicyList:
222				e.policyList(f.getPolicies(c))
223			case changeFieldBool:
224				e.boolTag(tagBool, f.getBool(c))
225			}
226		}
227	}
228	
229	func (e *fingerprintEncoder) decisionRecord(d *DecisionRecord) {
230		e.tag(tagDecisionRecord)
231		if d == nil {
232			return
233		}
234		// Field order and the subject/resource/decision group markers all come
235		// from the single decision field table, so the fingerprint, the UTF-8
236		// decision and the archive enumerate fields in exactly one place. No
237		// request or decision field is skipped.
238		for i := range decisionFields {
239			f := &decisionFields[i]
240			if f.groupTag != 0 {
241				e.tag(f.groupTag)
242			}
243			switch f.kind {
244			case decisionFieldString:
245				e.rawString(f.getString(d))
246			case decisionFieldStringList:
247				e.stringList(f.getList(d))
248			case decisionFieldBool:
249				e.boolTag(tagBool, f.getBool(d))
250			case decisionFieldInt:
251				e.int64Tag(tagSeq, int64(f.getInt(d)))
252			}
253		}
254	}
255	
256	// encodeCanonical returns the raw bytes fingerprinted for a record whose
257	// strings include invalid UTF-8. Every string the record carries reaches
258	// the output byte-for-byte, at whatever nesting depth or list position it
259	// occupies. The prefix separates this encoding space from JSON
260	// fingerprints. The outer fields come from the single record field table,
261	// so this encoding enumerates exactly the envelope members the JSON
262	// encoding and the valid-UTF-8 scan see, in the same order.
263	func encodeCanonical(r *AuditRecord) []byte {
264		e := &fingerprintEncoder{buf: []byte(rawEnvelopePrefix)}
265		e.tag(tagEnvelope)
266		for i := range recordFields {
267			f := &recordFields[i]
268			if f.jsonKey == "" {
269				// The record's own fingerprint is never an input to itself.
270				continue
271			}
272			switch f.kind {
273			case recordFieldString:
274				e.rawString(f.getString(r))
275			case recordFieldInt:
276				e.int64Tag(tagSeq, int64(f.getInt(r)))
277			case recordFieldChange:
278				e.change(f.getChange(r))
279			case recordFieldDecision:
280				e.decisionRecord(f.getDecision(r))
281			}
282		}
283		return e.buf
284	}
285	
286	// genesisFingerprint derives the chain root from the organization name,
287	// keeping equal identifiers in different organizations independent.
288	func genesisFingerprint(org string) string {
289		sum := sha256.Sum256([]byte("darksafe-audit-genesis\x00" + org))
290		return hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])
291	}
292	
293	// encodeJSONEnvelope renders the fingerprint envelope of a record whose
294	// strings are all valid UTF-8 as the exact byte sequence the historical
295	// encoding/json envelope struct produced: the envelope members in the
296	// single record field table's order, every string, integer and payload
297	// encoded by encoding/json itself, and the two payload members dropped
298	// when absent exactly as their historical omitempty tags did. Walking the
299	// table keeps this object in lockstep with the raw canonical encoding, the
300	// valid-UTF-8 scan and the archive framing by construction.
301	func encodeJSONEnvelope(r *AuditRecord) []byte {
302		var buf []byte
303		buf = append(buf, '{')
304		first := true
305		for i := range recordFields {
306			f := &recordFields[i]
307			if f.jsonKey == "" {
308				// The record's own fingerprint is never an input to itself.
309				continue
310			}
311			var (
312				value []byte
313				err   error
314			)
315			switch f.kind {
316			case recordFieldString:
317				value, err = json.Marshal(f.getString(r))
318			case recordFieldInt:
319				value, err = json.Marshal(f.getInt(r))
320			case recordFieldChange:
321				c := f.getChange(r)
322				if c == nil {
323					continue
324				}
325				value, err = json.Marshal(c)
326			case recordFieldDecision:
327				d := f.getDecision(r)
328				if d == nil {
329					continue
330				}
331				value, err = json.Marshal(d)
332			}
333			if err != nil {
334				// All envelope values are plain, JSON-encodable values; a
335				// failure here indicates a programming error, not user input.
336				panic(fmt.Errorf("darksafe: audit envelope must encode: %w", err))
337			}
338			if !first {
339				buf = append(buf, ',')
340			}
341			first = false
342			buf = append(buf, '"')
343			buf = append(buf, f.jsonKey...)
344			buf = append(buf, '"', ':')
345			buf = append(buf, value...)
346		}
347		return append(buf, '}')
348	}
349	
350	// fingerprintFor returns the fingerprint for a record. Records made
351	// exclusively of valid UTF-8 keep the historical JSON fingerprint, so old
352	// exports and checkpoints remain valid; records containing invalid bytes
353	// use the length-prefixed raw encoding that protects their exact bytes.
354	// Both families cover exactly the envelope members of the single record
355	// field table — never the record's own fingerprint.
356	func fingerprintFor(r *AuditRecord) string {
357		if recordUsesRawBytes(r) {
358			sum := sha256.Sum256(encodeCanonical(r))
359			return hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])
360		}
361		sum := sha256.Sum256(encodeJSONEnvelope(r))
362		return hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])
363	}
364	
365	// clonePolicies returns a detached copy of a policy set.
366	func clonePolicies(in []Policy) []Policy {
367		if in == nil {
368			return nil
369		}
370		return append([]Policy(nil), in...)
371	}
372	
373	// cloneChange returns a detached copy of a policy-change payload.
374	func cloneChange(c *PolicyChange) *PolicyChange {
375		if c == nil {
376			return nil
377		}
378		cp := *c
379		// Detach every list the single policy-change field table carries; the
380		// per-list nil-versus-empty handling stays exactly as clonePolicies
381		// defines it.
382		cloneChangeLists(&cp, c)
383		return &cp
384	}
385	
386	// cloneStrings returns a detached copy of a string slice while preserving
387	// its nil-versus-empty shape: a nil slice stays nil, and every non-nil
388	// slice, including a non-nil empty slice that still carries spare capacity,
389	// receives its own backing array. Copying only when len > 0 is not enough:
390	// a caller may submit make([]string, 0, 4), and aliasing that array into a
391	// stored record would let an append to one handed-out copy overwrite the
392	// first element of every other copy that shares it.
393	func cloneStrings(in []string) []string {
394		if in == nil {
395			return nil
396		}
397		return append([]string{}, in...)
398	}
399	
400	// cloneDecision returns a detached copy of a decision payload.
401	func cloneDecision(d *DecisionRecord) *DecisionRecord {
402		if d == nil {
403			return nil
404		}
405		cp := *d
406		// Detach every list the single decision field table carries, on non-nil
407		// rather than on len > 0 so empty-but-capacious lists are independent
408		// copies too; nil lists stay nil.
409		cloneDecisionLists(&cp, d)
410		return &cp
411	}
412	
413	// cloneRecord returns a fully detached copy of a record.
414	func cloneRecord(r *AuditRecord) *AuditRecord {
415		cp := *r
416		cp.Change = cloneChange(r.Change)
417		cp.Decision = cloneDecision(r.Decision)
418		return &cp
419	}
420	
421	// appendAuditLocked validates, fingerprints and stores one record. It runs
422	// under the store mutex and is the single place records are created.
423	func (st *orgState) appendAuditLocked(org, kind string, change *PolicyChange, decision *DecisionRecord) *AuditRecord {
424		seq := len(st.audit) + 1
425		prev := genesisFingerprint(org)
426		if len(st.audit) > 0 {
427			prev = st.audit[len(st.audit)-1].Fingerprint
428		}
429		// Store detached copies; later caller mutation must not reach the chain.
430		rec := &AuditRecord{
431			Org:             org,
432			Seq:             seq,
433			Kind:            kind,
434			Change:          cloneChange(change),
435			Decision:        cloneDecision(decision),
436			PrevFingerprint: prev,
437		}
438		rec.Fingerprint = fingerprintFor(rec)
439		st.audit = append(st.audit, rec)
440		return cloneRecord(rec)
441	}

443	// auditHeadLocked returns the highest sequence in the chain and the
444	// fingerprint that covers it: (0, genesis) for an organization with no
445	// records.
446	func (st *orgState) auditHeadLocked(org string) (int, string) {
447		if len(st.audit) == 0 {
448			return 0, genesisFingerprint(org)
449		}
450		last := st.audit[len(st.audit)-1]
451		return last.Seq, last.Fingerprint
452	}
453	
454	// Checkpoint pins an audit query to an exact point in a chain.
455	type Checkpoint struct {
456		Org         string
457		EndSeq      int
458		Fingerprint string
459	}
460	
461	// AuditPage is one stable slice of an organization's audit chain.
462	type AuditPage struct {
463		Org     string
464		Records []AuditRecord
465		// BeginSeq/EndSeq delimit the whole pinned range, not just this page.
466		BeginSeq int
467		EndSeq   int
468		// Next is the first sequence of the following page, 0 when exhausted.
469		Next int
470		// Checkpoint is the pinned upper bound shared by every page.
471		Checkpoint Checkpoint
472	}
473	
474	// recordMatches reports whether a record survives the query filters. Every
475	// set filter is a conjunction: kind, subject and resource conditions must
476	// all hold. Empty filter values mean "not set".
477	func recordMatches(r *AuditRecord, kind, subjectID, resourceID string) bool {
478		if kind != "" && r.Kind != kind {
479			return false
480		}
481		if subjectID != "" {
482			// A subject filter selects decision records of that subject only.
483			if r.Kind != AuditDecision || r.Decision == nil ||
484				r.Decision.Request.Subject.ID != subjectID {
485				return false
486			}
487		}
488		if resourceID != "" {
489			// A resource filter selects decision records whose request named
490			// exactly this resource. Policy-change records never match, even when
491			// a published policy carries the identical ResourceID: the condition
492			// reads the requested resource, not policy content. The comparison is
493			// Go string equality over the stored raw bytes, so case, surrounding
494			// and internal spaces, control bytes and invalid UTF-8 are all
495			// significant, and no path or wildcard is interpreted.
496			if r.Kind != AuditDecision || r.Decision == nil ||
497				r.Decision.Request.Resource.ID != resourceID {
498				return false
499			}
500		}
501		return true
502	}
503	
504	// optionalResourceCondition extracts the optional resource condition passed
505	// as the trailing variadic argument. An absent argument or an empty string
506	// means "no resource filter"; supplying more than one condition is a caller
507	// error rather than a silently picked value.
508	func optionalResourceCondition(conds []string) (string, error) {
509		switch len(conds) {
510		case 0:
511			return "", nil
512		case 1:
513			return conds[0], nil
514		default:
515			return "", fmt.Errorf("%w: at most one resource condition may be set, got %d", ErrInvalidPage, len(conds))
516		}
517	}
518	
519	// AuditQuery pins the first page of an audit query. startSeq is the first
520	// sequence considered (1 from the beginning); endSeq <= 0 means "everything
521	// currently stored". The returned checkpoint must be passed to AuditPage
522	// for the following pages, so records appended after the first query never
523	// mix into later pages.
524	//
525	// kind and subjectID are the existing optional filters (empty means unset):
526	// kind selects a record category and subjectID selects one subject's
527	// decision records. The optional trailing resourceID adds a resource
528	// condition, empty or absent meaning unset: only decision records whose
529	// requested resource ID equals it byte-for-byte survive — case sensitive,
530	// spaces and control bytes significant, no path or wildcard interpretation,
531	// invalid UTF-8 kept as-is — and policy-change records never survive it,
532	// even when a published policy names the same resource ID. Every set
533	// condition applies together. A resource filter changes only which records
534	// are returned: paging, checkpoints and detached copies behave exactly as
535	// without it, and omitting it preserves the historical call and its results.
536	func (s *Store) AuditQuery(org string, startSeq, pageSize int, kind, subjectID string, resourceID ...string) (*AuditPage, error) {
537		resource, err := optionalResourceCondition(resourceID)
538		if err != nil {
539			return nil, err
540		}
541		if org == "" {
542			return nil, ErrMissingOrganization
543		}
544		if kind != "" && kind != AuditPolicyChange && kind != AuditDecision {
545			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: unknown category %q", ErrInvalidPage, kind)
546		}
547		if pageSize <= 0 {
548			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: page size must be positive, got %d", ErrInvalidPage, pageSize)
549		}
550		if startSeq < 1 {
551			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: start sequence must be >= 1, got %d", ErrInvalidPage, startSeq)
552		}
553		s.mu.Lock()
554		defer s.mu.Unlock()
555		st := s.orgLocked(org)
556		end, fingerprint := st.auditHeadLocked(org)
557		cp := Checkpoint{Org: org, EndSeq: end, Fingerprint: fingerprint}
558		if end == 0 {
559			// An organization with no records always yields the empty genesis
560			// page, regardless of where the caller asked to begin.
561			return &AuditPage{Org: org, BeginSeq: 1, EndSeq: 0, Checkpoint: cp}, nil
562		}
563		if startSeq > end {
564			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: start sequence %d is beyond end sequence %d", ErrInvalidRange, startSeq, end)
565		}
566		return s.auditPageLocked(org, startSeq, end, fingerprint, pageSize, kind, subjectID, resource), nil
567	}
568	
569	// AuditPage returns one page of a previously pinned query. nextSeq is the
570	// cursor from the previous page; when it is 0 the range is exhausted. The
571	// checkpoint is re-verified against the chain on every call.
572	//
573	// The filters are the same as AuditQuery's and must agree with the pinned
574	// query: pass the same kind, subjectID and optional resourceID on every
575	// page. The resource condition is an exact raw-byte match over requested
576	// resource IDs and excludes policy-change records, exactly as on the first
577	// page; omitting it keeps the historical call and result shape.
578	func (s *Store) AuditPage(cp Checkpoint, nextSeq, pageSize int, kind, subjectID string, resourceID ...string) (*AuditPage, error) {
579		resource, err := optionalResourceCondition(resourceID)
580		if err != nil {
581			return nil, err
582		}
583		if cp.Org == "" {
584			return nil, ErrMissingOrganization
585		}
586		if kind != "" && kind != AuditPolicyChange && kind != AuditDecision {
587			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: unknown category %q", ErrInvalidPage, kind)
588		}
589		if pageSize <= 0 {
590			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: page size must be positive, got %d", ErrInvalidPage, pageSize)
591		}
592		if nextSeq < 0 {
593			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: next sequence must be >= 0, got %d", ErrInvalidPage, nextSeq)
594		}
595		s.mu.Lock()
596		defer s.mu.Unlock()
597		st, ok := s.orgs[cp.Org]
598		if !ok {
599			// No organization state: the only valid checkpoint is an empty one.
600			g := genesisFingerprint(cp.Org)
601			if cp.EndSeq == 0 && cp.Fingerprint == g && nextSeq == 0 {
602				return &AuditPage{Org: cp.Org, BeginSeq: 0, EndSeq: 0, Checkpoint: cp}, nil
603			}
604			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: checkpoint organization has no records", ErrInvalidRange)
605		}
606		head := len(st.audit)
607		if cp.EndSeq < 0 || cp.EndSeq > head {
608			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: end sequence %d beyond %d", ErrInvalidRange, cp.EndSeq, head)
609		}
610		wantFP := genesisFingerprint(cp.Org)
611		if cp.EndSeq > 0 {
612			if cp.EndSeq > len(st.audit) {
613				return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: end sequence %d beyond %d", ErrInvalidRange, cp.EndSeq, head)
614			}
615			wantFP = st.audit[cp.EndSeq-1].Fingerprint
616		}
617		if cp.Fingerprint != wantFP {
618			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: checkpoint fingerprint does not match the chain at sequence %d", ErrInvalidRange, cp.EndSeq)
619		}
620		if nextSeq == 0 {
621			return &AuditPage{Org: cp.Org, BeginSeq: 1, EndSeq: cp.EndSeq, Checkpoint: cp}, nil
622		}
623		if nextSeq > cp.EndSeq+1 {
624			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: next sequence %d beyond pinned range ending at %d", ErrInvalidRange, nextSeq, cp.EndSeq)
625		}
626		if nextSeq == cp.EndSeq+1 {
627			return &AuditPage{Org: cp.Org, BeginSeq: nextSeq, EndSeq: cp.EndSeq, Checkpoint: cp}, nil
628		}
629		return s.auditPageLocked(cp.Org, nextSeq, cp.EndSeq, wantFP, pageSize, kind, subjectID, resource), nil
630	}
631	
632	// auditPageLocked scans forward collecting up to pageSize matching records
633	// and computes the next-page cursor. It does not stop at pageSize raw
634	// records: filtering happens within the pinned [start,end] window, so
635	// non-matching records between matches — including policy changes excluded
636	// by a resource condition — never consume page slots.
637	func (s *Store) auditPageLocked(org string, startSeq, endSeq int, endFP string, pageSize int, kind, subjectID, resourceID string) *AuditPage {
638		st := s.orgs[org]
639		// pageSize only bounds how many records this page returns; it must not
640		// drive allocation. A caller may pass any positive value, including the
641		// largest int, for a range holding a handful of records, so preallocate
642		// no more than the window can actually contain.
643		window := endSeq - startSeq + 1
644		capHint := pageSize
645		if window < capHint {
646			capHint = window
647		}
648		out := make([]AuditRecord, 0, capHint)
649		i := startSeq
650		for ; i <= endSeq && len(out) < pageSize; i++ {
651			r := st.audit[i-1]
652			if recordMatches(r, kind, subjectID, resourceID) {
653				out = append(out, *cloneRecord(r))
654			}
655		}
656		next := 0
657		if i <= endSeq {
658			next = i
659		}
660		return &AuditPage{
661			Org:        org,
662			Records:    out,
663			BeginSeq:   startSeq,
664			EndSeq:     endSeq,
665			Next:       next,
666			Checkpoint: Checkpoint{Org: org, EndSeq: endSeq, Fingerprint: endFP},
667		}
668	}
669	
670	// AuditExport returns detached copies of the complete records through
671	// endSeq, suitable for offline verification. endSeq <= 0 means everything
672	// currently stored. An organization with no records yields an empty slice
673	// together with its sequence-0 checkpoint.
674	func (s *Store) AuditExport(org string, endSeq int) (records []AuditRecord, cp Checkpoint, err error) {
675		if org == "" {
676			return nil, Checkpoint{}, ErrMissingOrganization
677		}
678		s.mu.Lock()
679		defer s.mu.Unlock()
680		st := s.orgLocked(org)
681		head := len(st.audit)
682		if endSeq <= 0 {
683			endSeq = head
684		}
685		if endSeq > head {
686			return nil, Checkpoint{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: end sequence %d beyond %d", ErrInvalidRange, endSeq, head)
687		}
688		if endSeq < 0 {
689			return nil, Checkpoint{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: end sequence must be >= 0, got %d", ErrInvalidPage, endSeq)
690		}
691		// The checkpoint fingerprints the final exported record, not the
692		// possibly later current head.
693		fingerprint := genesisFingerprint(org)
694		if endSeq > 0 {
695			fingerprint = st.audit[endSeq-1].Fingerprint
696		}
697		out := make([]AuditRecord, 0, endSeq)
698		for i := 0; i < endSeq; i++ {
699			out = append(out, *cloneRecord(st.audit[i]))
700		}
701		return out, Checkpoint{Org: org, EndSeq: endSeq, Fingerprint: fingerprint}, nil
702	}
703	
704	// VerifyAudit validates an exported record set entirely without a Store.
705	// The caller separately retains the organization, end sequence and
706	// fingerprint they expect. It rejects any modified field, missing middle or
707	// tail record, swapped order, and record spliced in from another
708	// organization. Empty or nil records validate exactly when the checkpoint
709	// is the organization's genesis (end sequence 0).
710	func VerifyAudit(org string, records []AuditRecord, cp Checkpoint) error {
711		if org == "" {
712			return ErrMissingOrganization
713		}
714		if cp.Org != "" && cp.Org != org {
715			return fmt.Errorf("%w: checkpoint organization %q does not match %q", ErrInvalidRange, cp.Org, org)
716		}
717		genesis := genesisFingerprint(org)
718		if len(records) == 0 {
719			if cp.EndSeq != 0 || cp.Fingerprint != genesis {
720				return fmt.Errorf("%w: empty records but checkpoint claims end sequence %d", ErrInvalidRange, cp.EndSeq)
721			}
722			return nil
723		}
724		if cp.EndSeq != len(records) {
725			return fmt.Errorf("%w: have %d records, checkpoint ends at %d", ErrInvalidRange, len(records), cp.EndSeq)
726		}
727		prev := genesis
728		for i, r := range records {
729			wantSeq := i + 1
730			if r.Org != org {
731				return fmt.Errorf("%w: record %d belongs to organization %q", ErrInvalidRange, wantSeq, r.Org)
732			}
733			if r.Seq != wantSeq {
734				return fmt.Errorf("%w: record %d has sequence %d", ErrInvalidRange, wantSeq, r.Seq)
735			}
736			if r.PrevFingerprint != prev {
737				return fmt.Errorf("%w: record %d breaks the chain", ErrInvalidRange, wantSeq)
738			}
739			wantFP := fingerprintFor(&r)
740			if r.Fingerprint != wantFP {
741				return fmt.Errorf("%w: record %d fingerprint mismatch", ErrInvalidRange, wantSeq)
742			}
743			if r.Kind == AuditPolicyChange {
744				if r.Change == nil || r.Decision != nil {
745					return fmt.Errorf("%w: record %d payload does not match its category", ErrInvalidRange, wantSeq)
746				}
747			} else if r.Kind == AuditDecision {
748				if r.Decision == nil || r.Change != nil {
749					return fmt.Errorf("%w: record %d payload does not match its category", ErrInvalidRange, wantSeq)
750				}
751			} else {
752				return fmt.Errorf("%w: record %d has unknown category %q", ErrInvalidRange, wantSeq, r.Kind)
753			}
754			prev = r.Fingerprint
755		}
756		last := records[len(records)-1]
757		if last.Fingerprint != cp.Fingerprint {
758			return fmt.Errorf("%w: checkpoint fingerprint does not match the final record", ErrInvalidRange)
759		}
760		return nil
761	}
762	
763	// RecheckDecision re-evaluates the request stored in an organization's
764	// decision record against the policy version that decision actually used.
765	// Later publishes or rollbacks cannot alter the result. Non-decision
766	// records and missing sequences return distinguishable errors.
767	//
768	// The record and the version snapshot come exclusively from this
769	// organization's own live history; the version-zero and historical-policy
770	// judgment itself is shared with RecheckDecisionOffline in
771	// replayRecordedDecision.
772	func (s *Store) RecheckDecision(org string, seq int) (Decision, error) {
773		if org == "" {
774			return Decision{}, ErrMissingOrganization
775		}
776		if seq < 1 {
777			return Decision{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: sequence %d", ErrAuditNotFound, seq)
778		}
779		s.mu.Lock()
780		defer s.mu.Unlock()
781		st, ok := s.orgs[org]
782		if !ok || seq > len(st.audit) {
783			return Decision{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: organization %q has no audit sequence %d", ErrAuditNotFound, org, seq)
784		}
785		rec := st.audit[seq-1]
786		if rec.Kind != AuditDecision || rec.Decision == nil {
787			return Decision{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: sequence %d is %s", ErrAuditNotADecision, seq, rec.Kind)
788		}
789		req := rec.Decision.Request
790		version := rec.Decision.Decision.Version
791		resolve := func(version int) versionPolicies {
792			src, ok := st.versions[version]
793			if !ok {
794				// A decision's version is immutable and never deleted; its
795				// absence indicates store tampering rather than normal
796				// operation.
797				return versionPolicies{status: replayVersionAbsent}
798			}
799			// Live snapshots are immutable; detach anyway so the returned
800			// decision can never share storage with the store.
801			return versionPolicies{policies: append([]Policy(nil), src...)}
802		}
803		d, status := replayRecordedDecision(org, req, version, resolve)
804		if status == replayVersionAbsent {
805			return Decision{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: decision used version %d, which no longer exists", ErrVersionNotFound, version)
806		}
807		return d, nil
808	}

13	// payloads, the previous fingerprint — followed by the record's own
